sectionTitle: What changed beyond the sales office

primary.headline: Foreclosure Looms for Georgetown Housing Project With Unfinished Homes (Rocking Wilco / Onx Homes)
primary.summary: The planned 921-home Rocking Wilco subdivision in Georgetown, built by Onx Homes using a modular/tech-forward construction method, has sat with dozens of unfinished, abandoned homes since construction halted roughly nine months ago. The project is now headed to a foreclosure auction after no buyer stepped in to take over the site, per reporting corroborated by KXAN and KVUE.
primary.buyerImplication: A builder abandoning a subdivision mid-construction is one of the clearest new-construction buyer-trust failures this market has seen in 2026: buyers under contract or already closed in Rocking Wilco are now dealing with an unfinished, foreclosure-bound neighborhood, and the builder (Onx Homes) is not positioned to complete the work. It is a concrete illustration of why builder financial stability and track record matter as much as price or incentives.
primary.buyerAction: Before contracting with any builder -- especially a newer, smaller, or tech-forward entrant -- check how long they have operated in the Austin market, whether they have completed prior subdivisions start-to-finish, and whether their earnest money/deposit structure protects you if construction stalls. Ask directly about the builder's financial backing and request to see other completed communities in person, not just renderings.
primary.confidence: High on the underlying story (Austin American-Statesman, corroborated by KXAN and KVUE). Exact publication date is approximate, placed in the week of 2026-11-10 to 2026-11-15; recommend a human spot-check.
